reviews.text: I evaluated Aster, a relatively new layer-1 blockchain project launched in early 2024, focused on scalable DeFi and NFT ecosystems with an emphasis on low fees and high throughput. It uses a proof-of-stake consensus and integrates with EVM for easy developer adoption. The team is backed by venture capital from Asia, but it's still gaining traction amid market volatility. As of 2025, it has partnerships with a few dApps, but adoption is limited compared to established chains. Overall, it's promising for niche use cases like gaming but lacks the network effect of giants like Ethereum.

Perp Dex, a platform operating on the BSC network (EVM), Binance Labs and APX Finance are investors (https://icodrops.com/astherus   https://cryptorank.io/ico/astherus). Its token is aster. From his tweets, we can tell that Binance founder CZ is behind his platform. Even in adverse market conditions, we see that its price remains strong, which somewhat supports this. Documents indicate that the platform is subject to Hong Kong law (https://docs.asterdex.com/about-us/aster-privacy-policy) . This is a Dex operating exclusively on the BSC network. While not my style, it can make eccentric price movements.

After reviewing it with several resources, I can say Aster is a multichain decentralized exchange (DEX) focusing on perpetual and spot trading with very high leverage. It launched in September 2025 and quickly became famous, when its token surged also because of the support from CZ, creating a lot of rumors.
Aster multichain support is available on BNB Chain, Ethereum, Solana, Arbitrum and its own privacy-centric Aster Chain. Key features include MEV-resistant “hidden orders” for privacy, dual trading modes and yield-bearing collateral. If I should use only a phrase to identify the protocol I can say: “Aster is like a turbo multi-chain perpetual DEX, with degen leverage and unique privacy functionalities.” But to be honest, at the end, it’s essentially a self-custody trading platform trying to merge CeFi usability with DeFi.

The project presents a decentralized perpetual exchange. In its present stage it came as a result of the merger of two projects Astherus and Apx finance. The platform bridges DeFI with traditional markets, making a seamless platform that is non custodial.

I view Aster as an ambitious on chain exchange that’s pushing the limits on speed and leverage. It can be exciting to see how it offers extremely low fees and crazy leverage, but I’m also cautious its aggressive design could backfire if things go wrong.

I spent some time going through Aster and honestly, it looks like a solid project. Nothing too loud or over hyped, just a clean idea with a team that seems to be doing their work. I like how simple everything feels. The project looks organized and the direction is clear.
It’s still early though, so some parts feel a bit empty or not fully built yet, but I didn’t notice anything suspicious. Just a normal project trying to grow. If they keep pushing, it could turn into something good.
